On Sat, Nov 29, 2025 at 10:02 AM Samantha Kim <samantha.kim@orchard.ai> wrote:
> The 10k DAU is bursty...
> We'll implement a lightweight prefix cache...

Thanks for the detail, Samantha — this is super helpful. A few operational clarifications from the infra/ops side: 

- Batch size: for Redwood this refers to the server-side continuous batching window we use to pack concurrent requests on the GPU. Going from batch size 1 to ~4-6 reduces per-token cost materially (lower kernel overhead + better memory utilization). We'll provide a conservative estimate below.
- Cache semantics: prefix cache hit rate is most impactful when the cached prefix is long (>=32 tokens). For short prefixes the cost savings are smaller because completions still generate many tokens.
- Prefetching: if Orchard materializes likely completions client-side for a subset of prompts, we can effectively increase apparent hit-rate — please share which prompts you expect to prefetch.

I've attached an ops playbook excerpt that shows how we measure effective tokens/response and how we compute the tokens-per-dollar in practice.

Attachment: ops_playbook.pdf (section: token accounting + batching sensitivity)

Karthik — can you run the bursty concurrency profile through our quick simulator and paste back a rough tokens/$ delta for batch sizes 1, 3, 6? If we can get that in-line I'll add it to the MAP so Orchard has a clear economic tradeoff table.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: MAP — initial unit-econ assumptions and ask

Hi all — ran the quick sim against the profile Samantha sent (peak 1.2k concurrent). High-level numbers (rounded):

- Batch size = 1: effective tokens/response = 265, tokens per dollar = ~28,500 tokens/$
- Batch size = 3: effective tokens/response = 262, tokens per dollar = ~39,100 tokens/$
- Batch size = 6: effective tokens/response = 259, tokens per dollar = ~46,700 tokens/$

Notes: these assume no prefix cache. At 20% prefix cache hit rate (average cached prefix length 40 tokens) tokens/$ improves by roughly 12–16% depending on batch size. Prefetching the top 50 prompts at client-side increases effective hit rate to ~30% and yields a further ~6–8% improvement.

I'll attach the simulation snippet as a small markdown table in case you want to paste it into the MAP.

Attachment: MAP_cost_snippet.md (batching/caching sensitivity table)

Karthik
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
